classification.difficultyReason: Convert compass and reverse bearings to establish the right angle, then use the scaffolded distance and angle calculations to reconstruct the clockwise bearing of the final displacement and its reciprocal.

content.prompt: A ship leaves point $M$ and travels $300\text{ km}$ to point $P$, on a bearing of $N65^\circ E$. It then turns to travel $400\text{ km}$ at a bearing of $S25^\circ E$ to the point $Q$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the size of $\angle MPQ$?

answer.worked:
The true bearing of $P$ from $M$ is $065^\circ$, so the reverse bearing of $M$ from $P$ is $245^\circ$. The true bearing of $Q$ from $P$ is $180^\circ-25^\circ=155^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle MPQ&=245^\circ-155^\circ\\\angle MPQ&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How far is the ship now from its original position?

answer.worked:
Triangle $MPQ$ is right-angled at $P$. By Pythagoras' theorem,
$$\begin{align*}MQ^2&=MP^2+PQ^2\\MQ^2&=300^2+400^2\\MQ^2&=250000\\MQ&=500\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find $\angle PQM$, to the nearest degree.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Hence, find the true bearing of $Q$ from $M$ and the true bearing of $M$ from $Q$, to the nearest degree.

answer.short:
$118^\circ$ and $298^\circ$, respectively.

Add the angle at $M$ to $065^\circ$, then use the reverse bearing.
answer.worked:
Retain the unrounded angle from part (c).
$$\begin{align*}\angle PMQ&=90^\circ-\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac34\right)\end{align*}$$
The direction $MQ$ is clockwise from $MP$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing of }Q\text{ from }M&=65^\circ+90^\circ-\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac34\right)\\\text{Bearing of }Q\text{ from }M&\approx118^\circ\\\text{Bearing of }M\text{ from }Q&=65^\circ+90^\circ-\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac34\right)+180^\circ\\\text{Bearing of }M\text{ from }Q&\approx298^\circ.\end{align*}$$
